The study provides insights into the evolving autonomy of language models.

items.title: Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
items.contentSnippet:
Article URL: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/mozilla/internet-policy/apple-ios-browser-engine-rules/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50575644
Points: 355
# Comments: 209
items.creator: lapcat

summaries.zh: iOS上仍无非WebKit浏览器的主要原因是苹果的严格限制。苹果要求所有iOS浏览器使用其提供的WebKit引擎，禁止使用其他引擎。这一政策源于苹果对浏览器性能、安全性和一致性的考量。尽管有厂商尝试开发替代方案，但苹果的封闭策略使得非WebKit浏览器难以实现。Mozilla等公司呼吁苹果放宽限制，但截至目前，该政策仍未改变。
summaries.en: The article explains why non-WebKit browsers remain unavailable on iOS. Apple's strict policies require browsers to use its WebKit engine, limiting competition. This restricts alternative browsers like Firefox, which rely on other engines. The lack of options forces users to stick with Safari, impacting choice and innovation. The article highlights Mozilla's advocacy for open browser standards but acknowledges Apple's control over the ecosystem. The situation underscores the challenges faced by third-party browser developers on iOS.

summaries.zh: 一项实验性疗法通过向三名胰腺癌患者注射病毒，成功阻止了病情进展。该疗法利用病毒感染癌细胞并引发免疫反应。初步结果显示出显著效果，但需更多研究验证其安全性和有效性。目前该项目仍在早期阶段，未来可能为胰腺癌治疗提供新途径。
summaries.en: A clinical trial testing a virus injection to treat pancreatic cancer showed promising results in three patients, halting tumor growth. The therapy uses a modified virus to target and kill cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue. While the sample size is small, the findings suggest potential for further development. The study highlights the virus's ability to replicate in cancer cells, triggering an immune response. Additional research is needed to evaluate long-term effects and broader applicability. The trial represents a step forward in pancreatic cancer treatment options.
